claims.title: Browser-local Computer identity and draft continuity
claims.claim: Four local Computer IDs survive reload; two selected Computers retain distinct exact Code/Chat drafts. Retired-editor events, observed competing saves and a malformed identity record do not overwrite the protected tested records.
claims.limits: Browser-local namespaces only; two draft scopes exercised, not four independent runtimes or transactional cross-tab guarantees.

claims.title: Embedded document continuity and stale-message handling
claims.claim: Duplicate boot does not clear an active Files selection; child reload changes document correlation while retaining pin/context. Tested retired boot, navigation and command messages cannot replace current Code content or saved navigation.
claims.limits: Typed same-origin UI correlation, not authentication, grants, durable session authority or a comprehensive security audit.

claims.title: Early browser input and newer-choice precedence
claims.claim: The existing startup modules exercise held boot/commands, real dock/menu/keyboard/close actions, exact draft/editor retention and reload. A newer parent choice takes precedence over a delayed initial command.
claims.limits: The tests inject delivery schedules. Only the exercised startup orders in this Chromium environment are established.

claims.title: GOAL-aligned desktop geometry and pinned draft
claims.claim: At 1536x1024, both outer panes are 704x654 CSS pixels; four 335x214.5 tiles form a 2x2 grid with original forest wallpaper. Workspace-wide progress/audio placement and visible pinned Code text beside a changed left context pass independent observations.
claims.limits: One desktop viewport. No pixel-exact design, accessibility, responsive, cross-browser, physical fleet, live agent or execution certification. Reference metrics remain illustrative.
